comment: A pixel on one object, in the image the grounder looked at. A detector asked for "the cup"
cannot tell which cup; this says which. Backends that take points use it directly, the rest
use it to choose among their own boxes.

fields.name: phrase
comment: The grounded phrase this point belongs to.

fields.name: x
comment: Pixel column and row.
Six-DoF grasps for one object perception is already reporting. No imagery in the request: only
the server knows which mask belongs to which tracked object.

fields.name: object_id
comment: A class_id on /objects, indexed ("red_block_0") or the bare phrase ("red_block").

constants.name: HAND_LEFT
comment: Which hand the grasps are for; grasps do not transfer between hands.

fields.name: message
comment: Why there are none. An unknown object lists what is being reported; an unsupported hand is
refused, never mirrored.

fields.name: header
comment: Frame of every pose below, and the stamp of the depth frame they came from.

fields.name: grasps
comment: Best first, as poses of the GENERATOR's gripper frame, which is not in this robot's URDF: the
consumer applies its measured offset to reach its own grasp frame.

fields.name: scores
comment: Confidence in [0, 1], one per grasp.
One turn of the policy loop: the task in, the next chunk of joint targets out. Every policy
engine serves this and nothing else, which keeps them interchangeable.

fields.name: instruction
comment: Natural-language task.

fields.name: new_episode
comment: First request of a goal. A retry repeats the instruction verbatim, so the engine cannot infer
the boundary, and a stochastic head only resamples once its history is cleared.

fields.name: message
comment: Why no chunk could be produced. Empty when ok.

fields.name: chunk
comment: Absolute positions for any subset of the arm and hand joints; time_from_start must increase.
Turns an instruction into phrases an open-vocabulary detector can take. The detector wants a
short noun phrase and cannot parse "the mug left of the bowl"; a model that sees the scene can.

fields.name: phrases
comment: Short noun phrases, one or two attributes each, no relations.

fields.name: target_phrase
comment: The phrase the instruction is about, i.e. what to pick up.

fields.name: header
comment: Frame and capture time of the image the points below index into.

fields.name: exemplars
comment: Optional: a backend that cannot point returns none.
Close the last gap to a measured object after navigation has parked the robot nearby. Nav2's
xy_goal_tolerance (0.5 m) is far wider than the arm's reach window.
One closed loop over the measured pose, in x, y and yaw at once. The gait ignores small linear
commands, so the server floors its speeds rather than letting a proportional term fade out.

fields.name: object_id
comment: A class_id on /objects. Read when the goal starts, so a retry never replays a stale pose.

fields.name: working_yaw
comment: Heading to hold while approaching, rad, in the odometry frame. Pass the staging NavigateToPose
goal's yaw: re-aiming at the object from a metre out walks in on a curve.

fields.name: use_current_heading
comment: Hold the heading the robot arrived with and ignore working_yaw.

fields.name: timeout_s
comment: Seconds before giving up. 0 uses the server's default.

constants.name: ARM_LEFT
comment: Which arm must reach it. Only picks the side of the pelvis the object should end up on.

fields.name: message
comment: On failure, the phase that failed and why. Not meant to be parsed.

fields.name: final_x_m
comment: Where the object ended up in the base frame, m.
Current phase, also the prefix of a failure message.
Grasp an object with one arm by running a learned policy, validating every chunk of its output
against the planning scene before any of it executes.

fields.name: instruction
comment: Natural-language task for the policy engine.

fields.name: object_id
comment: A class_id on /objects. Success is its measured lift, not the policy's say-so.

constants.name: ARM_LEFT
comment: Selects the arm group and the hand allowed to touch the octomap while grasping.

fields.name: message
comment: Chunk counters and the measured lift, or what stopped the skill. Not meant to be parsed.

fields.name: chunks_executed
comment: Chunks executed, and chunks rejected before the arm moved.
Pick a known object off a surface with one arm.
The pose is read from /objects when the goal starts, so a retry re-reads it rather than
replaying a stale one. An object not seen within the server's sighting memory fails the goal.

fields.name: object_id
comment: A class_id on /objects.

constants.name: ARM_LEFT
comment: Selects the arm group, its hand group and the palm to attach to.

fields.name: message
comment: On failure, the phase that failed and why. Not meant to be parsed.
Current phase, also the prefix of a failure message.
Put down whatever the given arm is holding.
The target is where the object ends up, not where the palm goes: only the server knows how the
object is held. It is transformed into the planning frame on arrival, so an odom goal survives
the robot walking.

fields.name: surface_object_id
comment: Place on top of this detected surface, ignoring `pose`. Preferred: /objects is in odom, the
frame the base approach parked against, and map drifts from odom by more than the arm's window.

fields.name: pose
comment: Where the object should end up, used only when surface_object_id is empty.
Reverse away from a surface far enough that the next motion does not drag the arm across it.
Reverses and stops, without turning: a navigation goal normally follows. Reverse shares the
gait's forward deadband, so the server commands it above that floor.

fields.name: distance_m
comment: Distance to end up from the start, m. The gait coasts a little after the command stops, so
expect slightly more.

fields.name: timeout_s
comment: Seconds before giving up. 0 uses the server's default.
Move a planning group to one of its named SRDF poses, so the behavior tree can say "tucked"
without carrying joint values in XML. Free-form goals belong to MoveIt's own interfaces.

fields.name: group
comment: A group in g1.srdf: left_arm, right_arm, both_arms, left_hand or right_hand.

fields.name: named_target
comment: A group_state of that group. An unknown name fails the goal rather than silently holding.
No feedback: the move completes or fails, and "still executing" is nothing a caller can act on.
Step the base out of the band where Nav2 counts it as touching an obstacle.
Nav2's footprint is a circle wider than the body, so the gait's drift can leave the robot inside
that radius of furniture it is still clear of, and from there every Nav2 motion refuses to start.
This turns in place, then walks straight out, forward or backward, the way that gets clear
soonest. Already clear, it succeeds without moving.

fields.name: clearance_m
comment: Distance to end up from the nearest obstacle in the local costmap, m; at most 0.7, all the
3 m rolling costmap can check past the longest step.

fields.name: timeout_s
comment: Seconds before giving up. 0 uses the server's default.

fields.name: clearance_m
comment: From the base to the nearest obstacle at the end, m.
